items.problem: CS0104 HttpClient ambiguity between System.Net.Http and Windows.Web.Http caused by ImplicitUsings
items.evidence: session-log.txt L8234-8249: 14+ CS0104 errors across 6 files (ContentSelector.xaml.cs, Scenario2-7.xaml.cs, AdaptiveMediaSourceHttpFilterLogger.cs). Also 2 CS0535 errors from cascading type resolution failure.
items.skill_search: Grepped MIGRATION-PATTERNS.md for 'HttpClient', 'System.Net.Http', 'Windows.Web.Http', 'ImplicitUsings' — no matches. Only CS0104 coverage is for LaunchActivatedEventArgs (Windows.UI.Xaml vs Microsoft.UI.Xaml namespaces).
items.root_cause: The skill's CS0104 section covers the Windows.UI.Xaml ↔ Microsoft.UI.Xaml namespace collision but not the System.Net.Http ↔ Windows.Web.Http collision. .NET SDK projects with <ImplicitUsings>enable</ImplicitUsings> (the default since .NET 6) auto-import System.Net.Http, which conflicts with Windows.Web.Http types used in UWP samples that do HTTP interception (IHttpFilter, HttpClient, HttpRequestMessage, HttpResponseMessage).
items.proposed_fix: Add a new subsection to MIGRATION-PATTERNS.md under 'Common build errors after the namespace rewrite': ### CS0104: 'HttpClient' is an ambiguous reference between System.Net.Http and Windows.Web.Http. Explain that .NET SDK projects auto-import System.Net.Http via ImplicitUsings, which conflicts with Windows.Web.Http. Fix: add <Using Remove="System.Net.Http" /> to an <ItemGroup> in the .csproj. Note that this applies to any UWP code using Windows.Web.Http types (HttpClient, HttpRequestMessage, HttpResponseMessage, IHttpFilter).
items.generalizes: Any UWP sample or app that uses the Windows.Web.Http networking stack (IHttpFilter, HttpClient for WinRT, etc.) will hit this exact ambiguity when migrated to a .NET SDK-style project with ImplicitUsings. This is very common in media streaming, authentication, and network interception scenarios.
